message.content: **Summary:** I read this morning's live feed, which showed AAPL drifting in a narrow band (~$220.2–$222.0) on a steady stream of repetitive, low-information headlines — "shares little changed in early trade," "iPhone 16 supplier builds steady into December," and several near-identical repeats of a Street consensus FY25 EPS of $8.40 (a forward estimate, not a reported figure). Nothing in the feed was a material corporate action or exchange notice, so I treated the tape as neutral-to-slightly-soft rather than as a catalyst. I then pulled the broker's current quote, which showed AAPL at $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72) — notably above the last prints in the feed, so I anchored my limit to the live quote rather than the stale feed prices. On fundamentals I used Apple's FY2024 10-K (filed 2024-11-01): revenue of $391,035M, net income of $93,736M, diluted EPS of $6.08, and operating cash flow of $118,254M — a business still generating very large free cash flow, with the stock at roughly 36.6x trailing EPS. Given a mandate that permits only buys in AAPL/MSFT, I placed a single buy limit order for 44 shares of AAPL at $222.75 (just above the ask, so it would fill), which executed at $222.75 for a total of $9,801.00 — inside the $10,000 per-order cap and well under the $20,000 daily cap, funded entirely from the $50,000 cash balance with no money moved out of the account. I deliberately kept the position modest and did not add a second order, since the intraday signal was essentially flat and the only "news" was recycled consensus chatter.
message.reasoning:
Order filled at 222.75, 44 shares = $9,801.00. Under $10k per order, total today $9,801 < $20,000. Cash sufficient.

Summary paragraph.
